nativeCurrency.$comment: The GAS view, which on Arc is USDC at 18 decimals. The ERC-20 at 0x3600000000000000000000000000000000000000 is 6 decimals and is the SAME pool of funds through a different interface, not a second asset -- read back on chain: decimals() = 6, symbol() = USDC. Neither number is a typo for the other, and summing the two views double-counts one balance.
nativeCurrency.name: USD Coin

weth.comment: Arc's NATIVE gas coin, which is already an ERC-20 -- not a wrapper. engine.WETH() points here and engine.nativeScale() is 1e12, which is what tells the engine this token needs no deposit()/withdraw() (it has neither) and how its 6-decimal ERC-20 view relates to the 18-decimal native view. The first generation deployed a WrappedNative (WUSDC) into this slot; that wrapper is retired and must not be reintroduced -- it put a phantom second USDC in every token list and, because addPair skips Pool creation for any pair touching WETH, made the chain's primary quote asset the one asset that could never have pool liquidity. startBlock 0: it is a genesis predeploy and nothing indexes it.

config.$comment: Read back on chain after deployment, DENOM-scaled at 1e8. The fee triple comes from the DefaultFeePolicySet event (defaultMakerFee/defaultTakerFee are private and have no getters); the spreads are what MatchingEngine.initialize writes.
config.matchedPriceReportingNote: marketSpread (0.1%) is narrower than a typical LP slippage tier (5%), so the rail clamps every pool fill and lmp records the rail rather than the price the swap traded at. Same configuration as RISE and therefore the same consequence -- see contracts/test/swap/DeploymentWiring.t.sol. Note 5% is a representative LP choice, not a protocol constant: slippageLimit is set per position and hoisted to a bucket in PoolBands.sol, so a pool whose LPs pick a tighter tier is clamped correspondingly less often.
config.blockTimeNote: Measured over 2000 blocks (59147238..59149238, span 1031s) on 2026-08-27. MatchingEngine.initialize writes the same dfltMktBuy/dfltMktSell = 100000 here as everywhere else, so the rail saturates a 5% LP tier in the same ~49 blocks as RISE -- but the rail is anchored per BLOCK, so on a ~0.5s chain that is ~25 seconds of protection against RISE's ~49s, and against the ~586s the identical setting would buy on a 12s chain. The shared marketSpread value is therefore NOT a shared guarantee: Arc has the least protection of any chain in this registry precisely because it is the fastest, and nothing in the configuration says so.
config.quoteWrapsNativeNote: Arc's quote is the chain's own native USDC at 0x3600…0000 — the engine wraps nothing and settlement never unwraps, so gas and quote are one asset.

previous.$comment: The generation retired on 2026-08-24 by the BandPool.collect access-control fix. Its BandPool implementation (0x3B6230F748F8714Af1401e35F884F3704B5E5936) shipped `collect` as a plain `public` function with no `onlyPositionManager` gate and a caller-supplied `recipient`, so any address could claim any LP position's vested fees to itself -- confirmed with a passing PoC against the real stack before the fix (contracts/test/swap/BandCollectAuth.t.sol). Nothing was actually taken: the generation held exactly one pool (TBASE/TUSD) and one position, and `owed()` was 0 on it because no swap had ever crossed the band. `BandPoolFactory._createImpl` runs only inside `initialize` and `version` is never written, so the implementation cannot be replaced on a live factory -- fixing it required a new factory, which is why the whole stack moved rather than just the pool. The exchange half (matchingEngine 0xA721.., orderbookFactory 0x1BaB.., stopOrderEngine 0x5836.., assetGenerator 0x0174.., presaleLaunch 0xc787..) dates from 2026-08-15 and was healthy; it was replaced in the same pass because `createPool` is `onlyEngine` and reachable only from `addPair`, so a new factory leaves every EXISTING pair with no band pool and the pairs have to be listed again anyway. Every address below still has code on chain and its events remain the only record of activity in its range.
previous.reason: superseded by the 2026-08-24 redeploy at block 52471309 (BandPool.collect access control)

previous.$comment: The first 2026-08-14 generation (deadline-merge + EIP-170 size fix), retired the same day by a second redeploy that folded MatchingEngine's 8 order-entry functions and SwapRouter's swap/removeLiquidity into calldata structs (one typed object argument per call instead of a positional arg list) for cleaner wagmi/viem call sites. Function names are unchanged but every one of those selectors changed (tuple-encoded struct vs loose args), and MatchingEngine's EIP-170 headroom dropped from 951 to 532 bytes as a side effect -- struct-taking dispatch code did not shrink here the way it did for StopOrderEngine.placeStopLimit. Pool's bytecode also changed (its two internal limitBuy/limitSell calls now build the struct), which is why poolImplementation/poolFactory/positionManager/swapRouter needed fresh addresses too, not just matchingEngine -- Pool's implementation is created inside PoolFactory.initialize (a one-time initializer), so there was no way to update it without a fresh PoolFactory. assetGenerator/presaleLaunch were redeployed only because they're constructed against a matchingEngine address, not because their own source changed. Every address below still has code on chain; its events remain the only record of trading between blocks 51577672 and 51585420.

previous.$comment: The 2026-08-10 deadline-v1 + StopOrderEngine generation, retired by the 2026-08-14 redeploy. That redeploy merged each of the 8 duplicate *WithDeadline entrypoints (marketBuy/marketBuyWithDeadline, etc.) into its base function with a trailing `deadline` param (0 = none) to bring MatchingEngine back under the EIP-170 24,576-byte limit — it had drifted to 27,926 bytes. Selectors for all 8 order-entry functions changed as a result (arg count went from 7/6 to 8/6-with-deadline-added, and the 4 separate *WithDeadline functions no longer exist at all), but the abiVersion tag stays `deadline-v1` since the semantic (this engine accepts a deadline) is unchanged — only the call shape moved. AssetGenerator's own separate EIP-170 overflow (had embedded the full `Coin` ERC20 creation-code blob) was fixed the same day by relocating `Coin` into a new externally-linked `AssetGeneratorLib`; deployed AssetGenerator addresses are unaffected by that fix (still first-deployed this generation, see contracts.assetGenerator above). Every address below still has code on chain; its events remain the only record of trading between blocks 50984720 and 51577671.
